sources.title: A view built on real data.
sources.body: NASA models illustrate the journey. The introductory crater terrain is original decorative geometry, not the selected location. The mission-control flight from Earth to the Moon is illustrative: Earth, the Moon and their distance are to scale, the spacecraft are enlarged and the Sun is shown closer at its true apparent size; it is not a computed trajectory. Scientific results use cached Horizons ephemerides and the verified LOLA terrain product.
sources.disclaimer: The introduction is an illustrative animation. Apollo is not shown as a historical south-pole mission. NASA does not endorse this application.

glossary.summary: Horizon, elevation and visibility — a short guide
glossary.horizonText: the angle of the terrain skyline in each compass direction.
glossary.elevationText: how high the Sun or Earth is above the local horizontal plane.
glossary.visibilityText: the modeled object clears that terrain skyline. Partial sunlight means only part of the Sun's disk is visible. Earth-center visibility does not guarantee a communication link.
glossary.note: Differences describe this model and interval, not a safe landing recommendation. Fine time sampling does not remove terrain uncertainty.

serverText.Watch sunlight cross the local horizon: Watch sunlight cross the local horizon
serverText.Sampled terrain-relative visibility esti: Sampled terrain-relative visibility estimates, not landing safety or a radio link budget. Short windows do not establish permanent light or shadow. Unknown coverage is not darkness. This is a sky/horizon lesson at one observer, not a surface-wide moving-shadow simulation.
serverText.A ridge can hide a low Sun even when it: A ridge can hide a low Sun even when it is above the reference horizontal plane.
serverText.Change the date, keep the place: Change the date, keep the place
serverText.Compare these two 24-hour windows. A sho: Compare these two 24-hour windows. A short window cannot establish permanent illumination or permanent shadow.
serverText.Earth is not a ground station: Earth is not a ground station
serverText.Seeing Earth's centre is only a geometri: Seeing Earth's centre is only a geometric condition; antennas, stations and a link budget are not modeled.
serverText.Geometric line of sight only; not a guar: Geometric line of sight only; not a guaranteed radio link.
serverText.Generic DSN elevation limit; station-spe: Generic DSN elevation limit; station-specific horizon masks are not applied.
serverText.Antenna keyhole, station scheduling, ava: Antenna keyhole, station scheduling, availability and link budget are not modeled.
serverText.Earth visibility refers to the Earth cen: Earth visibility refers to the Earth center above the local terrain horizon.
serverText.Spherical Moon with point-mass gravity (: Spherical Moon with point-mass gravity (GM 4902.800118 km^3/s^2, JPL DE440); no mascons or J2.
serverText.Planar motion in the orbit plane; lunar: Planar motion in the orbit plane; lunar rotation (about 0.4 m/s at 85 deg S) is neglected.
serverText.Initial orbit is circular; descent orbit: Initial orbit is circular; descent orbit insertion is an impulsive Hohmann burn to 50 000 ft above the site.
serverText.Gates and phase durations follow the Apo: Gates and phase durations follow the Apollo 11 premission profile (NASA TN D-6846, Table I).
serverText.Closed-loop ZEM/ZEV guidance to each gat: Closed-loop ZEM/ZEV guidance to each gate, not the Apollo P63/P64 flight software; no hover or redesignation.
serverText.Engine: constant specific impulse; TN D-: Engine: constant specific impulse; TN D-6846 throttle rule (10-60 % of design thrust, else fixed throttle position).
serverText.Plane changes are impulsive in the initi: Plane changes are impulsive in the initial orbit, before descent orbit insertion.
serverText.Terrain clearance along the descent path: Terrain clearance along the descent path is not checked.
serverText.Each route reuses the R4 model: planar p: Each route reuses the R4 model: planar point-mass Moon, Hohmann DOI, ZEM/ZEV guidance through the Apollo 11 gates.
serverText.Variants change only the initial orbit a: Variants change only the initial orbit altitude and the approach and terminal-descent durations; gate states stay at Apollo 11 values.
serverText.Propellant is counted from DOI ignition;: Propellant is counted from DOI ignition; the DOI mass is backed out from the PDI mass for the 60 n.mi. reference orbit.
serverText.The reserve is propellant left at touchd: The reserve is propellant left at touchdown sufficient for the reserve delta-v at the landing mass (rocket equation).
serverText.Hover margin is the hover time the prope: Hover margin is the hover time the propellant above the reserve buys at the landing mass (thrust = weight, constant Isp).
serverText.Assessment time (approach + terminal des: Assessment time (approach + terminal descent) is the time available to see and assess the landing area; it is a planning proxy for safety, not a probability of success.
serverText.Enable 'include descent' to add R4/R5 re: Enable 'include descent' to add R4/R5 reachability and fuel.
serverText.No validated science-value dataset is in: No validated science-value dataset is integrated yet.
serverText.Only sampled candidate starts are evalua: Only sampled candidate starts are evaluated; shorter windows between starts may be missed.
serverText.Lower is closer: mean of sunlight shortf: Lower is closer: mean of sunlight shortfall / 100 percentage points, excess darkness / mission hours, and Earth shortfall / mission hours. Equal weights; ties by UTC start then job ID. Not a safety ranking.
serverText.Solar flares cannot be predicted with ce: Solar flares cannot be predicted with certainty; SWPC gives daily probabilities for at most 3 days.
serverText.Analysis time outside the SWPC forecast: Analysis time outside the SWPC forecast days has no forecast; nothing is extrapolated.
serverText.Current conditions describe the Sun when: Current conditions describe the Sun when the snapshot was fetched, not at the landing time.
serverText.GOES measures near Earth; proton flux is: GOES measures near Earth; proton flux is a proxy for the lunar surface, not a dose estimate.
serverText.The radio blackout scale describes HF ra: The radio blackout scale describes HF radio on Earth's sunlit side, not DSN links.
